chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, reporting it from a man from the general Muslims, who said:
I used to sit in a gathering of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so by Allah, I had not seen a gathering nobler than his gathering.
He said to me one day, 'From where does the sneeze come out?' So I said, 'From the nose'. So he said to me: 'You are wrong'.
So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! From where does it come out?' So he said: 'From the entire body, just as the sperm comes out from the entire body, and its exit is from the urethra'.
Then he said: 'Have you not seen the person when he sneezes, his body parts shake? And the sneezer is safe from death for seven days'.
ai.seo_question: Where does a sneeze originate from according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical nature of sneezing by comparing its origin to that of semen, illustrating how a universal bodily essence exits through a specific channel. This narration highlights the Shia understanding of the body as a unified entity where spiritual and physical states intersect, linking the physical act of sneezing to divine protection from death for seven days. The hadith serves as a reminder of the interconnectedness of bodily functions and spiritual well-being in Islamic physiology.
